sections: 107.1.c.1, 718.5.e-g and 719.3: attached gear can have a different controller and follows the bearer
190.3.a.2 and 323: control change, contested status and cleanup
355 and 356: targets, optional additional costs and finalization
Recall: base destination differs from Move

implementation_contract: Track ownership independently from the current controller. Return, Kill, Banish and Recycle use the owner for non-Board destinations; Recall uses the current controller's base.
Possession chooses an enemy unit at a battlefield. On resolution it changes control then Recalls that same physical object. It does not implicitly Ready, Exhaust, Heal, Play or Move it.

Conscription declares an optional 5 XP additional cost before payment. Without that choice its target must have at most 3 Might; paying widens the target requirement. Resolve control, Exhaust and Recall in printed order.

Recheck the appropriate live target requirements after responses. Losing the battlefield or enemy requirement can invalidate the target. A paid optional cost remains attached to the play across staged payment and rollback.

Attached gear keeps its controller and owner when its bearer changes control. It still contributes Might and effect text, follows the bearer even into the opposing base, and detaches normally on departure. Its printed Equip ability is inactive while attached; an applicable permission such as Weaponmaster may allow reattachment. After detachment its controller can use Equip normally.

A pending ability retains its controller after its source changes control. Board references must retain physical identity across control changes, while live friendly/enemy and location requirements are rechecked.
Existing object statuses and applicable duration restrictions persist through control changes; leaving the board and replaying creates a new board object.

Record contested status for control changes at battlefields, then apply cleanup after the full resolving action. Conscription and Possession Recall before that cleanup; do not invent an intermediate combat.
Conservation checks must reconstruct each owner's cards across both controllers' board areas. Tokens disappear on leaving the board and are not physical deck cards.
Expose controller, owner and cross-controller attachments consistently in API observations, native inspection and coaching. Use public information only.
scope: Adds source evidence for two additional Chaos practice options, not a claim of current Irelia metagame prevalence.
The current source catalog marks both cards Standard-legal; the November 23 announcement is already represented in format_updates.json and does not name these cards.
No runtime card or sourced preset is added by this review.
Spell control, temporary control, and gear control require further source-specific implementation; these are not certified by permanent unit control.
